newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ economic activity slips in Sept qtr - NBNZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ economic activity slips in Sept qtr - NBNZ.

text.p: Economic activity in New Zealand slipped 0.2 percent in the September quarter, the first quarterly decline in 5 1/2 years, the National Bank of New Zealand said on Wednesday.
NBNZ's Regional Trends survey showed nine regions recorded a drop in economic activity, led by large falls in Waikato, Hawke's Bay, Auckland and the West Coast.
Economic activity fell 0.3 percent in the North Island while the South Island recorded a 0.2 percent increase.

At a national level the key economic indicators to decline included real estate turnover, retail trade, dwelling approvals and new commercial motor vehicle registrations. Rises were measured in business confidence, employment, consumer confidence and new car registrations.
NBNZ said economic activity rose three percent in the country as a whole in the year to September. The North Island recorded a 3.3 percent rise, while the South grew by only 1.9 percent.
Wellington moved into the top-ranked position in September, with year-on-year growth rising to a two year high of 4.3 percent.

"This was the first time that the region has held the top ranking since the heady days of 1986/87, and is a reversal from its slump in 1991-93 when Wellington recorded the lowest ranking for eight consecutive quarters," NBNZ said.
